Work

Case study, IriusRisk

How many CI containers a test suite needs

End-to-end tests ran in 7 CI containers, one per product module. My first model balanced them and was 42% faster in a one-worker test run, but only about 8% with the 5 workers production used. Modelling the workers showed that 4 containers would be faster than 7 and cost 41% less.

Read the case study about how many CI containers a test suite needs

Things I've built

  • CI Shard Advisor

    I turned the pipeline idea into a public tool. It reads Cypress run reports and recommends how to split the test files across containers so that the slowest one finishes as early as possible. For most inputs nobody knows the right answer in advance, so I test its core with property-based, metamorphic and invariant tests.

    Open the live demo ↗ (opens in a new tab) Code on GitHub for CI Shard Advisor ↗ (opens in a new tab)

  • Screen Recorder (QA mode)

    I built this Chrome extension for my own bug reports. It records console logs and network requests along with the video, and saves each step with a Cypress or Playwright selector ready to paste into a test. I test it against a bug bench I built, a page that breaks on demand.

How I test

There's a saying in software that perfect is the enemy of good. It always grated on me a little. In maths, where I started, a proof is either right or wrong, and I think that's partly why I ended up in QA.

I check that it does what it should

Nobody can prove that software has no bugs. I check each feature against what it's meant to do and automate those checks so problems show up early. At Fieldeas I moved the team from manual testing to automation.

How this site is tested →

A bug stays open until I know why

When something breaks, I keep digging until I understand the cause. I write down what I learn in my QA Wiki.

Read the QA Wiki ↗ (opens in a new tab)

My bug reports come with the evidence

A bug report should give the developer what they need to reproduce the bug. When the screen recorder I used for mine changed, I built my own Chrome extension to capture that evidence.

How I built the recorder →

I check what AI tells me

AI tools are part of my work, and I use them carefully. On my wiki, the AI answer button replies only from articles I wrote, and it cites the ones it used.
